news.title: Fifa reportedly allowed DR Congo into World Cup despite ineligible player in qualifying
news.lede: Nigeria filed complaint over ineligible players in playoff. Fifa investigators aware of situation before tournament. Fifa allowed the Democratic Republic of the Congo to compete at this summer’s World Cup despite reports suggesting an internal investigation found that the country had fielded an ineligible player in qualifying. The player in question, the goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, starred for his nation at the tournament, including against England in the last 32.

news.title: He did not complete the procedure to play for Congo, but FIFA allowed him to play in the World Cup.
news.lede: The International Football Federation (FIFA) knew before the World Cup that Congolese goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi was ineligible when he played in several qualifying matches, but allowed him to continue playing in the tournament held this summer in the USA, Canada and Mexico, world media reported today. The New York Times and the French daily Le Monde cited internal FIFA documents on the Mpasi case, further intensifying the focus on the disciplinary procedures of the world football body under president Gianni Infantino. As reported, the 32-year-old Mpasi was a member of the French under-17 national team, but never completed the procedure before FIFA for a change, that is, for the right to play for Congo, with which he has family ties.

news.title: Who is Anirudh Thapa? The Indian footballer who ended 44-year wait for a goal against two-time World Cup
news.lede: India may have suffered a heavy 6–1 defeat to Uruguay in Kolkata, but one moment still gave the home crowd something significant to celebrate. Anirudh Thapa's equaliser against the two-time FIFA World Cup champions ended a 44-year wait for an Indian goal against La Celeste, placing the midfielder alongside a player from a very different era of the national team's history. Anirudh Thapa's equaliser against Uruguay marks a significant moment in Indian football history, ending a 44-year wait for a goal against the two-time World Cup champions. Discover Thapa's journey and impact on the Indian national team.

news.title: Lionel Messi has completed football and can bid Argentina farewell with pride
news.lede: Messi says goodbye with 208 caps and a World Cup but there were times he thought his glory would never come. Not for the first time, Lionel Messi is returning to the Argentina national team. This occasion, however, will be accompanied by a sense of completion and celebration rather than obligation, as the country bids farewell to probably the greatest footballer ever. Messi will wear the Argentina shirt one last time this week for a friendly in Buenos Aires against Benin after he was invited back for a celebratory runout following his decision to retire from international football after the World Cup final.

news.title: One Day to Go: CAF Strategy Conference set to bring Africa’s football leadership together in Cabo Verde
news.lede: With one day to go, preparations are complete in Sal, Cabo Verde for the CAF Strategy Conference, which will bring together Africa’s football leadership, National Team coaches and international football experts from 07-09 October 2026. Convened under the leadership of CAF President Dr Patrice Motsepe, the three-day gathering in Santa Maria, Sal Island, will focus on strengthening the development and sustainability of African football while drawing important lessons from the continent’s historic performance at the FIFA World Cup 2026. FIFA President Gianni Infantino is among the leading international football figures expected in Cabo Verde, alongside Presidents of CAF’s 54 Member Associations, CAF Executive Committee members, Zonal Union Presidents, senior Men’s, Women’s and Youth National Team coaches and international football experts.

news.title: From a red card after 47 seconds to kissing the World Cup: the incredible story of Messi that changed Argentine football forever.
news.lede: Lionel Messi's first adventure with the Argentina National Team lasted just 47 seconds. The final performance will begin more than 21 years later, in front of a packed Monumental stadium and with a country ready to say goodbye. Between those two images fits practically an entire footballing life: defeats that seemed definitive, a resignation that shocked the world, nights of redemption and, finally, the scene that for years seemed impossible: Messi lifting the World Cup. This Tuesday, against Benin, the number 10 will put on the albiceleste jersey for the last time.

news.title: 'I wish he was African', Benin coach on facing Messi in last Argentina game
news.lede: Lionel Messi will earn his 208th cap for Argentina in the friendly against Benin. Twenty-one years after Lionel Messi helped Argentina beat Nigeria in the Under-20 World Cup final, another African side will be on the pitch for the final match of his international career. Benin face Argentina at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday in a farewell match for the 39-year-old. For Benin assistant coach Tunde Adelakun, there is a neat symmetry to the occasion.
